reason: The text explicitly portrays the Hebrews as followers of Yahweh through multiple direct references: (1) God identifies Himself as 'יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵי הָעִבְרִיִּים' (Yahweh, God of the Hebrews); (2) God reaffirms His covenant relationship by declaring He is 'אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב' (God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob), indicating continuity of worship across generations; (3) The text shows God's paternal concern for 'עַמִּי' (My people), the Hebrews, and His commitment to their liberation; (4) The Hebrews themselves invoke 'לַיהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ' (Yahweh our God), explicitly identifying Yahweh as their deity; (5) The passage concludes with the people's belief and worship: 'וַֽיַּאֲמֵן הָעָם' and 'וַֽיִּקְּדוּ וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲוּוּ' (the people believed and they bowed down and worshiped), demonstrating their status as active followers of Yahweh.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
